nodes.title: Classification & IUPAC Nomenclature
points: Classification by number of halogens: Mono, di (geminal / alkylidene dihalide vs vicinal / alkylene dihalide), tri, and polyhaloalkanes.
Classification by C(sp³)-X bond: Alkyl (1°, 2°, 3°), Allylic (X bonded to sp³ C next to C=C: CH₂=CH−CH₂−X), Benzylic (X bonded to sp³ C attached to aromatic ring: C₆H₅−CH₂−X).
Classification by C(sp²)-X bond: Vinylic (X bonded directly to sp² carbon of C=C: CH₂=CH−X), Aryl halides / haloarenes (X bonded directly to aromatic ring: C₆H₅−X).
IUPAC rules: Longest carbon chain selected containing halogen; numbered to give lower locants to substituents/halogens (haloalkanes).

formulas.label: Geminal vs Vicinal dihalide structures
formulas.expr: Geminal: CH₃-CHX₂ (alkylidene dihalide) | Vicinal: CH₂X-CH₂X (alkylene dihalide)

formulas.label: Allylic vs Vinylic halide classification
formulas.expr: Allylic: CH₂=CH-CH₂-X (sp³ C) | Vinylic: CH₂=CH-X (sp² C)

nodes.title: Methods of Preparation of Alkyl Halides
points: From alcohols: 1) Lucas reagent (conc HCl + anhy. ZnCl₂): 3° > 2° > 1°; 2) Phosphorus halides: 3R−OH + PCl₃ → 3R−Cl + H₃PO₃; R−OH + PCl₅ → R−Cl + POCl₃ + HCl; 3) Darzens method: R−OH + SOCl₂ (pyridine) → R−Cl + SO₂↑ + HCl↑ (best method as gaseous by-products escape).

From alkenes: Markovnikov addition of HX (negative part adds to less hydrogenated C); Anti-Markovnikov addition (Peroxide / Kharasch effect: valid ONLY for HBr in presence of organic peroxides R−O−O−R).
Halogen exchange: 1) Finkelstein reaction: R−Cl / R−Br + NaI (dry acetone) → R−I + NaCl↓ / NaBr↓; 2) Swarts reaction: Synthesis of alkyl fluorides using metallic fluorides (AgF, Hg₂F₂, CoF₃, SbF₃).

formulas.label: Darzens thionyl chloride reaction (best method)
formulas.expr: R-OH + SOCl₂ (pyridine, Δ) → R-Cl + SO₂↑ + HCl↑

formulas.label: Finkelstein reaction (iodoalkane synthesis)
formulas.expr: R-Cl + NaI (dry acetone) → R-I + NaCl↓

formulas.label: Swarts reaction (fluoroalkane synthesis)
formulas.expr: CH₃-Br + AgF → CH₃-F + AgBr↓

formulas.label: Peroxide effect (Kharasch effect with HBr)
formulas.expr: CH₃-CH=CH₂ + HBr (peroxide) → CH₃-CH₂-CH₂-Br (1-bromopropane)

nodes.title: Physical Properties: Polarity, Boiling Point & Solubility
points: C−X bond polarity: Polar due to electronegativity difference (Cδ⁺ − Xδ⁻). Dipole moments: CH₃Cl (1.87 D) > CH₃F (1.82 D) > CH₃Br (1.81 D) > CH₃I (1.62 D). CH₃Cl > CH₃F because C−Cl bond length is significantly larger (μ = q × d).
Boiling points: Higher than corresponding alkanes due to dipole-dipole and dispersion forces. Order: R−I > R−Br > R−Cl > R−F (increasing molecular mass and polarizability).

Branching effect: For isomeric alkyl halides, boiling point decreases with branching (n-butyl > isobutyl > sec-butyl > tert-butyl) because branching makes molecule spherical, reducing surface area and van der Waals attractions.
Solubility: Insoluble in water because alkyl halides cannot form hydrogen bonds with water molecules and cannot break existing water H-bonds; soluble in organic solvents.

formulas.label: Order of boiling points (same alkyl group)
formulas.expr: R-I > R-Br > R-Cl > R-F (increasing molecular mass and polarizability)

formulas.label: Branching effect on boiling points
formulas.expr: n-butyl bromide (102 °C) > isobutyl bromide (91 °C) > tert-butyl bromide (73 °C)

formulas.label: Dipole moment order of methyl halides
formulas.expr: CH₃Cl (1.87 D) > CH₃F (1.82 D) > CH₃Br (1.81 D) > CH₃I (1.62 D)

nodes.title: Nucleophilic Substitution Reactions of Haloalkanes
points: Formation of alcohols: R−X + KOH(aq) → R−OH + KX.
Ambidentate nucleophile CN⁻: R−X + KCN(alc) → R−CN (alkane nitrile, C-attack); R−X + AgCN(alc) → R−NC (alkyl isocyanide / carbylamine, N-attack because AgCN is covalent).
Ambidentate nucleophile NO₂⁻: R−X + KNO₂(alc) → R−O−N=O (alkyl nitrite, O-attack); R−X + AgNO₂(alc) → R−NO₂ (nitroalkane, N-attack because AgNO₂ is covalent).
Other substitutions: With NH₃(alc) gives amines (Hoffmann ammonolysis); With R'COOAg gives esters; With R'ONa gives ethers (Williamson synthesis).

formulas.label: KCN vs AgCN substitution duality
formulas.expr: R-X + KCN(alc) → R-CN (nitrile) | R-X + AgCN(alc) → R-NC (isocyanide)

formulas.label: KNO₂ vs AgNO₂ substitution duality
formulas.expr: R-X + KNO₂(alc) → R-O-N=O (alkyl nitrite) | R-X + AgNO₂(alc) → R-NO₂ (nitroalkane)

formulas.label: Williamson ether synthesis
formulas.expr: R-X + R'O⁻Na⁺ → R-O-R' + NaX (best with 1° alkyl halide)

nodes.title: Mechanisms: S_N1 vs S_N2 & Stereochemistry
points: S_N2 (Bimolecular): Single-step, concerted backside attack via pentacoordinate transition state. Rate = k[R−X][Nu⁻] (2nd order). Complete inversion of configuration (Walden inversion). Reactivity: Methyl > 1° > 2° > 3° (steric hindrance controls rate). Favored by polar aprotic solvents (acetone, DMSO).

S_N1 (Unimolecular): Two steps. Step 1: Slow ionization forming planar carbocation (rate determining); Step 2: Fast attack of nucleophile from either side. Rate = k[R−X] (1st order). Results in racemization (mixture of retention and inversion). Reactivity: 3° > 2° > 1° > Methyl (carbocation stability controls rate). Favored by polar protic solvents (H₂O, ROH).
Leaving group ability: I⁻ > Br⁻ > Cl⁻ > F⁻ (weaker base = better leaving group).

formulas.label: S_N2 Rate Law and Reactivity
formulas.expr: Rate = k[R-X][Nu⁻] | Reactivity: CH₃X > 1° > 2° > 3° (Walden inversion)

formulas.label: S_N1 Rate Law and Reactivity
formulas.expr: Rate = k[R-X] | Reactivity: 3° > 2° > 1° > CH₃X (Planar carbocation, racemization)

formulas.label: Leaving group ability order
formulas.expr: I⁻ > Br⁻ > Cl⁻ > F⁻ (weaker conjugate base = better leaving group)

nodes.title: Elimination Reactions & Saytzeff's Rule
points: β-elimination (dehydrohalogenation): Alkyl halide heated with alcoholic KOH eliminates HX to produce an alkene.
Saytzeff's Rule (Zaitsev's Rule): In dehydrohalogenation of unsymmetrical alkyl halides, the more substituted (more alkylated, more stable) alkene is formed as the major product.
Example: Dehydrohalogenation of 2-bromobutane gives but-2-ene (81%, major, trans > cis) and but-1-ene (19%, minor).
Competition between substitution and elimination: 1° halides favor S_N2; 3° halides with strong bases or higher temperatures favor E2 elimination.

formulas.label: Dehydrohalogenation of 2-bromobutane
formulas.expr: CH₃-CH₂-CH(Br)-CH₃ + alc. KOH (Δ) → CH₃-CH=CH-CH₃ (81%, but-2-ene, major) + CH₃-CH₂-CH=CH₂ (19%, minor)

formulas.label: Saytzeff Rule statement
formulas.expr: Major alkene = alkene having greater number of alkyl substituents attached to doubly bonded carbons

nodes.title: Reactions with Metals: Grignard, Wurtz & Organometallics
points: Grignard reagent preparation: R−X + Mg (dry ether) → R−Mg−X (alkyl magnesium halide). C−Mg bond is polar covalent, Mg−X bond is ionic.
Moisture sensitivity: Grignard reagents react violently with compounds having active hydrogen (H₂O, ROH, RNH₂) to form alkanes (R−Mg−X + H₂O → R−H + Mg(OH)X). Hence dry ether is strictly required.
Wurtz reaction: 2R−X + 2Na (dry ether) → R−R + 2NaX (synthesizes symmetrical alkanes with even number of carbon atoms).
Frankland reaction: 2R−X + Zn (dry ether) → R−R + ZnX₂.

formulas.label: Grignard reagent preparation
formulas.expr: R-X + Mg (dry ether) → R-Mg-X (organometallic compound)

formulas.label: Grignard reaction with active hydrogen
formulas.expr: R-Mg-X + H₂O → R-H (alkane) + Mg(OH)X

formulas.label: Wurtz reaction for symmetrical alkanes
formulas.expr: 2R-X + 2Na (dry ether) → R-R + 2NaX

nodes.title: Haloarenes: Low Reactivity & Electrophilic Substitutions
points: Low reactivity towards nucleophilic substitution: 1) Resonance: C−Cl bond acquires partial double bond character; 2) Hybridization: C is sp² (more electronegative, shorter C−Cl bond 169 pm) vs sp³ in haloalkanes (178 pm); 3) Instability of phenyl cation.
Drastic conditions (Dow's Process): Chlorobenzene + NaOH (623 K, 300 atm, H⁺) → Phenol. Presence of electron-withdrawing −NO₂ groups at ortho/para positions increases reactivity drastically.

Electrophilic aromatic substitution: Halogen is ortho/para directing due to +R resonance, but deactivating due to strong −I inductive effect (chlorination, nitration, sulfonation, Friedel-Crafts alkylation/acylation; para isomer is major).
Reactions with metals: Wurtz-Fittig reaction (Ar−X + R−X + 2Na → Ar−R + 2NaX); Fittig reaction (2Ar−X + 2Na → Ar−Ar biphenyl + 2NaX).

formulas.label: Dow's process for chlorobenzene
formulas.expr: C₆H₅-Cl + 2NaOH (623 K, 300 atm) → C₆H₅-ONa (dil HCl) → C₆H₅-OH (phenol)

formulas.label: Wurtz-Fittig reaction
formulas.expr: C₆H₅-Br + CH₃-Br + 2Na (dry ether) → C₆H₅-CH₃ (toluene) + 2NaBr

formulas.label: Fittig reaction
formulas.expr: 2C₆H₅-Cl + 2Na (dry ether) → C₆H₅-C₆H₅ (biphenyl) + 2NaCl

nodes.title: High-Weightage Board Questions & Named Conversions
points: Board Q1: Distinguish between S_N1 and S_N2 mechanisms (kinetics, molecularity, steps, intermediate/transition state, stereochemistry, solvent, order of reactivity).
Board Q2: Explain why haloarenes are extremely less reactive towards nucleophilic substitution reactions.
Board Q3: Explain optical activity of 2-chlorobutane (presence of asymmetric/chiral carbon atom with 4 different attached groups: −H, −CH₃, −C₂H₅, −Cl).

Environmental and commercial uses: Freon-12 (CF₂Cl₂ aerosol propellant, depletes ozone layer); Chloroform (CHCl₃ stored in dark amber bottles filled to brim to prevent oxidation into poisonous phosgene gas COCl₂); Iodoform (CHI₃ yellow antiseptic solid liberating I₂); DDT (non-biodegradable insecticide).

formulas.label: Oxidation of chloroform to poisonous phosgene
formulas.expr: 2CHCl₃ + O₂ (light) → 2COCl₂ (phosgene gas) + 2HCl

formulas.label: Synthesis of DDT
formulas.expr: 2C₆H₅Cl + CCl₃-CHO (conc H₂SO₄) → (p-Cl-C₆H₄)₂CH-CCl₃ + H₂O

nodes.title: MHT-CET High-Speed Shortcuts & Elimination Hacks
points: TRAP 1: KCN vs AgCN: KCN forms Nitrile (R−CN, step-up reaction adding 1 carbon); AgCN forms Isocyanide (R−NC, same carbon chain length).
TRAP 2: KNO₂ vs AgNO₂: KNO₂ gives Alkyl nitrite (R−O−N=O); AgNO₂ gives Nitroalkane (R−NO₂).
TRAP 3: Kharasch effect operates ONLY with HBr (NOT with HCl or HI, as HCl H-Cl bond is too strong and HI addition step is endothermic).
TRAP 4: Neopentyl halide (CH₃)₃C−CH₂−X is primary (1°) but reacts extremely slowly via S_N2 due to massive steric crowding (neopentyl effect).
TRAP 5: Optical rotation of racemic mixture: [α] = 0° (optically inactive by external compensation of equimolar d- and l-enantiomers).

formulas.label: S_N1 reactivity order mnemonic
formulas.expr: 3° > 2° > 1° > CH₃ (follows carbocation stability: benzylic ≈ allylic > 3° > 2° > 1°)

formulas.label: S_N2 reactivity order mnemonic
formulas.expr: CH₃ > 1° > 2° > 3° (inversely proportional to steric hindrance at alpha carbon)

formulas.label: Racemic mixture optical inactivity
formulas.expr: [α]_mix = 0° (optically inactive by external compensation of d and l forms)
